title: What is the difference between AirElement \ FiberElement \ RadonElement ?
body:
seems like:
1. FiberElement is the normal DOM node in C++.
2. RadonElement is only used in List scenario. with the Radon Diff algorithm.
3. AirElement is the another DOM node type. But a much more simple one ?

so, might i ask, how is the performance of the radon diff algorithm, 
And, is the air DOM bring in a much faster UPP / ARP ? 💐💐💐

看起来是说：
1. FiberElement是一般意义下的DOM节点
2. RadonElement服务于列表场景，有一个Radon diff 算法来加速diff.
3. AirElement是另一个更轻量的DOM。

性能上，radon diff / air， 应该分别提升都挺大的，不过具体是多少呢 🤔 💐💐💐
author: Hippo0x0

comments.body:
It's a good question. 

RadonElement is the first Element implementation. At that time, we did not provide the Element PAPI to the framework, but instead offered the 'RadonNode PAPI' for the framework to create 'RadonNode' (which is a type of C++ VDOM). The engine executes the Diff algorithm with 'RadonNode', creates RadonElement based on the Diff results, and completes the subsequent pixeling.

Inspired by the community's 'NoDiff' frameworks, we also began to explore some NoDiff frameworks. The implementation of RadonElement is not very convenient for exposing the PAPI, so we started to design FiberElement and AirElement. The FiberElement and AirElement are similar; both can be considered as normal DOM nodes in C++. AirElement is used to quickly validate the performance of certain solutions, without having to consider compatibility with some previous implementations. The FiberElement is relatively a more long-term solution. From the very beginning of its design, we attempted to make it compatible with 'RadonNode', so that we could have an Element that supports both 'RadonNode' and Element PAPI in the future.

After some exploration, we now have a way to unify FiberElement, RadonElement, and AirElement into Element. We expect to complete this change in the near future.

As for performance issues, the use cases for each Element are different, so we haven't strictly compared the performance of each Element. During the integration process, we will consider this aspect and try to retain the advantages of all Elements as much as possible.


这确实是一个好问题

RadonElement 是我们最早期的 Element 实现，当时我们并没有提供 Element PAPI 给到框架，而是提供了 ‘RadonNode PAPI’ 让框架创建 RadonNode（本质上是一种 C++ VDOM）。所有的 Diff 逻辑由引擎执行，之后创建 RadonElement 完成后续的渲染

受社区的 'NoDiff' 框架启发，我们也开始探索一些 NoDiff 框架，RadonElement 的实现不太方便直接暴露 PAPI，所以我们开始着手设计 FiberElmenet 和 AirElement。AirElement 被用来快速验证一些方案的性能，不用考虑对于之前一些实现的兼容性。FiberElement 相对来说是一个更长期的方案，一开始设计时便尝试兼容 'RadonNode'，为了之后能够有一个 Elemnet 既能支持 ‘RadonNode’，又能支持 Element PAPI。

目前经过一些探索，配合前端框架，我们已经有办法将 FiberElement，RadonElement，AirElement 统一为 Element，这个改动仍在进行中。

至于性能问题，由于每一种 Element 的定位和使用场景是不一样的，所以我们没有严格对比过每一个 Element 的性能。我们在融合过程中，会考虑这一部分，尽可能保留所有 Elmenet 的优势。

title: [Infra][BugFix] handle concurrent vpython invocations from multiple process

title: [BugFix] Fix crash in SplitStringByCharsOrderly when input string con…
body:
## Summary

Here is a crash on Android.

> backtrace: 
    00 abort+164 
    01  std::__ndk1::__throw_out_of_range(char const*) at stdexcept:265 
            (inlined by) std::__ndk1::__basic_string_common<true>::__throw_out_of_range() const at string:616 
            (inlined by) std::__ndk1::basic_string<char, std::__ndk1::char_traits<char>, std::__ndk1::allocator<char> >::basic_string(std::__ndk1::basic_string<char, std::__ndk1::char_traits<char>, std::__ndk1::allocator<char> > const&, unsigned long, unsigned long, std::__ndk1::allocator<char> const&) at string:1952 
    02 std::__ndk1::basic_string<char, std::__ndk1::char_traits<char>, std::__ndk1::allocator<char> >& lynx::base::Vector<std::__ndk1::basic_string<char, std::__ndk1::char_traits<char>, std::__ndk1::allocator<char> > >::emplace_back<char const*&, unsigned long, unsigned long>(char const*&, unsigned long&&, unsigned long&&) at vector.h:616 
 (inlined by) lynx::base::SplitStringByCharsOrderly(std::__ndk1::basic_string_view<char, std::__ndk1::char_traits<char> >, char*, unsigned long) at string_utils.cc:393 
            (inlined by) auto lynx::base::SplitStringByCharsOrderly<(char)58, (char)59>(std::__ndk1::basic_string_view<char, std::__ndk1::char_traits<char> >) at string_utils.h:146 
    03 lynx::tasm::RendererFunctions::SetDynamicStyleTo(lynx::lepus::Context*, lynx::lepus::Value*, int) at renderer_functions.cc

```cpp
base::InlineVector<std::string, 32> SplitStringByCharsOrderly(
    std::string_view str, char cs[], size_t char_count) {
    const char* byte_array = str.data();
    const size_t size = str.size();
    ...
    grouper.emplace_back(byte_array, static_cast<size_t>(word_start), static_cast<size_t>(word_count));
}
```
The constructor that will be called in `emplace_back` here is `std::string(const std::string&, size_t, size_t)`.

If the input `str` contained a `\0` character, the implicit construction of `std::string` from `byte_array` would truncate at `\0`. 

If `word_start` is located after `\0`, an `out_of_range` exception will be thrown.

This fix ensures `std::string_view` is used instead, preserving the entire input and preventing unintended truncation.

- [x] Documentation updated (or not required).

title: Regarding minimum Android/iOS Version
body:
Hey,
so I am currently evaluating Lynx for a project of mine and the near-native performance et cetera looks really good.

Another point which may be a USP for Lynx is the minimum required API levels for iOS and Android
| Name | Min Android API level | Min. iOS Version |
|--------|--------|--------|
| Flutter | **21** | 12 |
| React Native (also Expo) | 24 | 15.1 |
| Lynx | **21** | **10** | 


Being able to support from iOS 10 and Android 5 upwards means that there are millions of devices which you can uniquely target with Lynx apps, especially in evolving markets, which would not be possible with React Native or Flutter.


I can imagine that ByteDance with their diverse user-base has an interest in upkeeping the support for older devices, but if someone could provide a statement on whether or not this support will be gradually dropped in newer versions with more features, just like React Native, or if this is an intended behaviour which you are trying to keep

(Obviously nobody is going to get on your nerves when you drop iOS 10 support in 2030 :) )

Thanx a lot in advance
author: AltayAkkus

comments.body: Lynx is a cross-platform framework that mostly shares logic between multiplatforms, and We basically do not rely on higher version apis on Android or iOS. Upgrading minimum Android/iOS version is something that requires careful consideration and detailed review for us.

That's great! 

I would suggest you guys to communicate this on your website, this is a really big benefit over Flutter and React Native, far more tangible than increased performance.

If I had to convince my boss to use Lynx over React Native, the argument that Lynx can address millions more customers would be great.
